content: Depo-Provera SubQ 104 is specifically indicated for the prevention of pregnancy in females of reproductive potential. The recommended dose is 104 mg administered subcutaneously every 12 to 14 weeks. For sexually active women with regular menstrual cycles, the first injection should only be administered during the first five days of a normal menstrual period. For breastfeeding women, the first injection should be given during or after the sixth postpartum week. Use of Depo-Provera SubQ 104 for more than two years is not recommended unless other birth control methods or medical therapies for endometriosis-associated pain are deemed inadequate. This limitation is due to the potential negative impact on bone mineral density (BMD) with long-term use. The intramuscular (IM) or oral (PO) forms of medroxyprogesterone have not been studied in this context, and no results are available. Acitretin decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone through an unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as contraceptive failure may occur. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives and may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Etrasimod and medroxyprogesterone may increase each other's effects due to immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. The additive immune system effects of etrasimod in combination with other immunosuppressive therapies have not been studied. Avoid coadministration during and in the weeks following etrasimod administration. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. Lesinurad decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional nonhormonal contraception, as hormonal contraception alone may not be reliable. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may reduce systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during coadministration and for four months after the last dose. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sugammadex decreases the effects of medroxyprogesterone by receptor binding competition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sugammadex may bind to progestogen, reducing its exposure. A sugammadex bolus dose is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients using oral contraceptives on the same day as sugammadex or those with transdermal or implant hormonal contraceptives should use additional nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) for the next seven days. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as medroxyprogesterone may impair glucose tolerance. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; use an alternative if available. Atazanavir and medroxyprogesterone may decrease each other's effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; use an alternative if available. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and hormonal contraceptive effectiveness may be diminished. Additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Crofeler increases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofeler inhibits CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit it systemically due to minimal absorption. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; use an alternative if available. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elagolix decreases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing the dose if needed. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events at elevated plasma concentrations. Encorafenib affects medroxyprogesterone by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or decrease efficacy. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Contraceptive failure is possible; use an alternative if available. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Medroxyprogesterone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination oral contraceptives have been shown to significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine metabolism.
